newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq sets plan to recharge German unit.
newsitem.headline: Compaq sets plan to recharge German unit.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said on Thursday it aimed to revive its German unit in 1997 by introducing a line of low-priced personal computers and focusing on sales to small and mid-sized businesses.
A new series of machines due in the next few months would sell for between 2,300 and 3,000 marks, Kurt Dobitsch, managing director of Compaq Computer GmbH, said at a new conference.
"This will give us another segment to play in," he said. "This segment will clearly become larger this year."
Dobitsch said Germany has two million small businesses and 21,000 mid-sized companies that have not installed PCs as quickly as large corporations.
Compaq was looking to form many new partnerships with small consultants who put together computer systems for accountants, doctors, and other types of small businesses.
He defined small businesses as having fewer than 100 employees, and mid-sized companies as having 100 to 500 employees.
German sales would also get help from recently introduced workstations and networking products, he said.
A workstation based on Intel Corp's Pentium Pro processor and Microsoft Corp's Windows NT operating system was released last year.
